questiontext.text: What does order_of_key(x) return?

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. It tells us how many elements come before x in sorted order, which is its rank.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

answer.text: The number of elements smaller than x

questiontext.text:
What does this program print?

main.cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <ext/pb_ds/assoc_container.hpp>
#include <ext/pb_ds/tree_policy.hpp>
using namespace std;
using namespace __gnu_pbds;
typedef tree<int, null_type, less<int>, rb_tree_tag, tree_order_statistics_node_update> ordered_set;

int main() {
    ordered_set s;
    s.insert(8);
    s.insert(3);
    s.insert(5);
    cout << *s.find_by_order(1) << endl;
    return 0;
}

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. The sorted elements are 3, 5, 8. The element at index 1 is 5.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

#include <iostream>

int main() {

questiontext.text:
What does this program print?

main.cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <ext/pb_ds/assoc_container.hpp>
#include <ext/pb_ds/tree_policy.hpp>
using namespace std;
using namespace __gnu_pbds;
typedef tree<int, null_type, less<int>, rb_tree_tag, tree_order_statistics_node_update> ordered_set;

int main() {
    ordered_set s;
    for (int x : {1, 2, 3, 2}) {
        s.insert(x);
    }
    s.erase(2);
    cout << s.size() << endl;
    return 0;
}

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. The second 2 is ignored because the set holds each value once. The set is {1, 2, 3}, and erasing 2 leaves {1, 3}: size 2.

incorrectfeedback.text: Not quite. Read the explanation below.

questiontext.text:
Match each term with its meaning.

Drag each description onto the item it belongs to.

Rank  →  [[1]]

Inversion  →  [[2]]

Median  →  [[3]]

pb_ds  →  [[4]]

Unique id  →  [[5]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. These are the words of the lesson.

The correct answer:

  • Rank → The number of elements smaller than a given one
  • Inversion → A larger element before a smaller one
  • Median → The middle element after sorting
  • pb_ds → A GCC extension that holds the ordered tree
  • Unique id → A number that tells equal copies apart

questiontext.text:
What does this program print?

main.cpp
int a[3] = {2, 3, 1};
int inv = 0;
for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    for (int j = i + 1; j < 3; j++) {
        if (a[i] > a[j]) {
            inv++;
        }
    }
}
cout << inv << endl;

Assume the needed #include lines and using namespace std; are already written.

generalfeedback.text: Explanation. The pairs (2,1) and (3,1) are inversions. The pair (2,3) is in order. So the count is 2.

questiontext.text:
Is the operation fast (about log n) in both, or only in the ordered set?

Drag the correct label next to every item.

Find the k-th smallest element  →  [[1]]

Count elements smaller than x  →  [[1]]

Find the rank of a value  →  [[1]]

Insert a value  →  [[2]]

Erase a value  →  [[2]]

Check whether a value exists  →  [[2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. A plain set must walk element by element to learn ranks, but both structures insert, erase and search in O(log n).

The correct answer:

Fast only in ordered_set: Find the k-th smallest element, Count elements smaller than x, Find the rank of a value
Fast in both: Insert a value, Erase a value, Check whether a value exists

questiontext.text:
Match each expression with its job.

Drag each description onto the item it belongs to.

s.order_of_key(x)  →  [[1]]

*s.find_by_order(k)  →  [[2]]

s.insert({x, id})  →  [[3]]

s.size() - s.order_of_key(x)  →  [[4]]

s.erase(s.lower_bound({x, -1}))  →  [[5]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. These expressions appear in the programs of the lesson.

The correct answer:

  • s.order_of_key(x) → The number of elements smaller than x
  • *s.find_by_order(k) → The value with rank k
  • s.insert({x, id}) → Adds a copy with a unique id
  • s.size() - s.order_of_key(x) → The number of seen elements not smaller than x
  • s.erase(s.lower_bound({x, -1})) → Erases one copy of x

questiontext.text:
Do we need pairs with ids here?

Drag the correct label next to every item.

Different student numbers  →  [[1]]

Inversions of a permutation  →  [[1]]

Running median of distinct readings  →  [[1]]

A leaderboard where scores repeat  →  [[2]]

Inversions of an array with repeated values  →  [[2]]

The k-th smallest of a list with repeats  →  [[2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Explanation. An ordered set drops repeated values. When equal values must all be kept, pairs with unique ids make them different.

The correct answer:

Distinct values are enough: Different student numbers, Inversions of a permutation, Running median of distinct readings
Needs pairs with ids: A leaderboard where scores repeat, Inversions of an array with repeated values, The k-th smallest of a list with repeats
